figures.finding: A guardian assists or represents the child in contractual matters; under Sectoral Determination 10 the employer of a child under fifteen must conclude the written contract with the parent, legal guardian or an agent they authorise in writing, who signs on the child's behalf, and the pay goes to the parent or guardian; no share of the earnings is required to be set aside.

value.binding: guardian's assistance or representation (Children's Act s. 18(3)(b)); for under-15s in advertising, artistic and cultural work, a written contract signed by the parent, legal guardian or written-authorised agent (SD 10 cl. 3)
value.payTo: the parent or legal guardian (SD 10 cl. 4)
value.reachesWritingDirecting: SD 10 reaches the 'performance' of advertising, artistic and cultural activities and counts an independent contractor as employed; writing or directing isn't named (reading)

sources.said: (b) assist or represent the child in administrative, contractual and other legal matters;
The parent, legal guardian or agent of the child must sign the contract of employment on behalf of the child

figures.finding: No one may employ a child under fifteen in advertising, artistic or cultural work without a permit from the Minister of Labour (Form SD 10.1, issued as SD 10.2, for a period and on conditions the Minister sets); a child over ten works at most four hours a day, one of ten or under three, and may be at the workplace at most ten, eight (over five) or six (under five) hours; a 30-minute break comes after two hours (over ten) or ninety minutes; night work (22:00-05:00) at most three times a week with the parent's written leave; the parent or child-minder may stay within sight and sound on a film, television or advertising set; and no one under eighteen may hold the permit.

value.issuer: Minister of Labour (delegable to the Director-General or an officer of Assistant Manager rank or higher)

night.needs: parent's written permission, written reasons, an agreed allowance

value.chaperone: parent, legal guardian or child-minder within sight and sound on film, television or advertising sets; accompanied when staying overnight
value.reachesWritingDirecting: no: the Determination covers the performance of advertising, artistic and cultural activities (reading)

figures.finding: The South African Guild of Actors admits any actor legally entitled to work in South Africa who is or is about to be engaged as an actor, a citizen being so entitled if registered as a taxpayer; it sets no minimum age.

value.eligibility: legally entitled to work in South Africa (a citizen registered as a taxpayer) and engaged or about to be engaged as an actor

sources.said: An actor who is ‘legally entitled to work in the Republic of South Africa' is defined as a citizen who is registered as a taxpayer ... 7.1. Any actor legally entitled to work in the Republic of South Africa shall be eligible for membership of SAGA, provided that such actor is, or is about to be engaged in the South African film/ television/theatre/radio industry as an actor.

figures.finding: The National Film and Video Foundation takes applications from individuals, companies and organisations; production funding is for South African production companies (or new filmmakers with a company attached) and development funding also for writers attached to a project; every applicant shows a South African ID and a tax clearance; no applicant age is stated on these pages.

value.production: South African production companies; new filmmakers with a production company attached
value.development: independent production companies holding rights or options for 12 months; writers attached to a project

figures.applies: 2026/27 funding call and the NFVF's funding pages, read 2026-11-01.

sources.said: Individuals, companies, and organisations may submit funding applications to the NFVF for any of the open funding categories stated above.

figures.finding: One or more persons may incorporate a profit company, but an unemancipated minor is ineligible to be a director, so a minor may hold shares but direct his company only from eighteen or once emancipated.
figures.applies: Companies Act 71 of 2008 as gazetted 9 April 2009; later amendments not read.
